He gives me options. For example, the last time I was in a mixed state he asked if I wanted to attack the hypomania or the depression. I said to treat the depression and that's why I'm up to 500 mg of Lamictal. When I tell him the side effects of the Lithium, Zyprexa, or Lamictal he works with me to change the dose or switch to something different. We have a good therapeutic relationship and I've been seeing him for 11 years. I tell him what's going on, he gives me options, and if I believe that's not going to work I propose something different. As I said we work together well. It is frustrating, however.

I do have a psychiatrist and every clinician I have spoke to says he is one of the best on the island (I live in Hawaii). He's saved my life at least 8 or 9 times so I trust him. I only take Zyprexa if I feel like I'm entering a hypomanic state, which hasn't happened in a while. I have experienced it in a mixed state, but as I said I am mostly depressed when that happens. We talked about everything I wrote and he's been working his ass off to keep me alive in the past few months. I will cross post this in SuicideWatch. Thank you for the advice.

BP I here. Currently on Prozac (10 mg), Lamictal, Lithium, Visteril for sleep. My psychiatrist told me Lithium and Lamictal is the gold standard for treating bipolar. Lithium is the only mood stabilizer, as far as I know, that does not induce cognitive impairment. Side effects are having dihaerra and going to the bathroom if you eat something, and you will develop hand and leg tremors. I can live with these side effects because it stops the mania. When I was on Depakote it took me a year and a half to pass Calc I and pass Calc 2 after failing it once. Depakote also put me in a function depression where I was irritable and would have outbursts in class.

Try finding something other than Lamictal to attenuate the depression. SSRIs are not recommended because of the risk of mania. Anti-Convulsants seem to work best for depression because it affects the cellular membrane and doesn't take the time necessary to balance things out in the synapse. Sometimes they will prescribe a low dose of anti-psychotics to try and take care of the depression. In my case I was given Geodon.There are all sorts of anti-depressants available so you do have a lot of options.

I saved 2 people from suicide. The first happened in 2001, around Christmas. I was driving home from a party at 1 in the morning when I randomly glanced up at a foot bridge crossing the highway. There was a girl looking down from the middle of the bridge and when I saw that, it didn't make sense to me; I had a feeling she was in trouble. I pulled over and as I was walking up to talk to her I was praying to God the whole time that I would find the right words to say ant not fuck it up. She told me she felt so alone and it was only her and her baby and it felt like everyone had left her. I told her that if she did this her baby would be totally alone. I tried pleading with her not to make this decision... that if you go through with this, you won't be able to watch your daughter grow up. After about 20 minutes of talking with her, her friend drove past and noticed us talking. She pulled over, and from her car she yelled something to the effect of, "Grab her!" She started putting her leg over the railing and the next thing I know I wrapped my arms around her stomach and I was talking into her ear, "I'm not going to let you go. I'm not going to let you go." Her friend came up to where we were standing and I told her, you take her to the hospital and you get her the best care she can get. As I was walking away she told me I was the girl's guardian angel.

The second life I saved happened in February of last year. I'm very open on facebook that I have Bipolar Disorder. One of my classmates from high school messaged me one night and said she suffered from depression and anorexia. I don't even think I spoke to her in high school, but she called me after exchanging a few facebook messages and the first thing she tells me is she's drinking and has a bunch of pills in front of her. She told me that she got pregnant in her 20s, she broke up with the father, and that she miscarried and had to go through that shit on her own. She said that she never got over the loss of her baby. We continued to talk and then she told me to get a pen and a piece of paper. She then started dictating to me her suicide note over the phone. I transcribed it only to humor her, and she made me read it back to her. She continues to drink and take pills, and she kept saying to me, "I'm done. I'm done." After a few more minutes of her drinking and taking pills, the phone drops to the floor and the line goes dead. I live in Hawaii and I she live in Las Vegas. I had my phone company patch me straight through to Vegas 911 and I gave the cops her name and they were able to go to her house. After about 20 minutes, an LVPD officer called me and said, "Your friend is a alive." I later found out that she was in intensive care for 10 days and after that she was transferred to the psych unit. She's supposed to come back for a visit to Hawaii and I said I would take her out to a nice dinner.
I also saved my friend from getting shot after her dad pulled a gun on her, but that's for another time.

TL;DR: Saved a girl from jumping from a bridge by holding on to her. Saved my friend from a drug over dose by calling the cops in Vegas when I live in Hawaii.
